name: search_wiki
title: Search the wiki
description: Search the user's wiki and return the most relevant page sections with their full text, best first, each with its page, the page's last edit date (to tell current notes from stale ones) and a link. Up to three sections come from the same page. Tasks that match are results too, with their status, tags, dates and notes.

query.description: What to look for: words or a question. Also: "exact phrase", -word to leave out, #tag for pages (frontmatter tags) and tasks with a tag, -#tag, and edited:2026-09 / after:2026-07-01 / before:2026-08 for when a page was last edited (a task: its last activity).

under.description: Only pages in this folder and its subfolders, without tasks, e.g. 'tickets' or 'projects' (the slug part before a '/').

notes.description: Only notes (the user's quick notes in Notes, not yet filed into the wiki), without tasks.

name: search_tasks
title: Search tasks
description: List the user's tasks, filtered by tag and status, each with its fields and a link. Without a query, open tasks come by deadline, then start date; done ones newest first. With a query, by relevance. Starts with today's date.

tag.description: Only tasks with this tag; several comma-separated tags must all match, e.g. 'leaf' or 'work,urgent'.

assignee.description: With users: only this user's: 'me' ("my tasks"), a user name, 'none', 'a|b', '-a'.

status.description: open, closed (done or won't do), or all.

query.description: Words to look for in title, description and tags; "exact phrase", -word and edited:/after:/before: (last activity, e.g. after:2026-09-01) work too.

order.description: deadline, or manual: the user's own order (priority)

name: grep_wiki
title: Find lines in the wiki
description: Find every line of every page that matches a regular expression, as page slug, line number and line: for exact text and all its occurrences (ticket ids, names, TODOs, an old term to replace), where search_wiki gives only the most relevant sections. Perl-style regex (\d, \b, (?:…), lookarounds); escape . ( [ and such to match them literally. Pages only, not tasks.

under.description: Only pages in this folder and its subfolders, e.g. 'tickets'.

limit.description: How many lines to show; the total is always given.

name: read_page
title: Read a page
description: Return a wiki page's full markdown, frontmatter included, by its slug, followed by the pages that link to it and its wikilinks that lead nowhere. With heading, only that section (subsections included): cheaper for long pages.

slug.description: The page's slug as search_wiki or list_pages give it, e.g. 'git-remote' or 'journal/2026-09'.

heading.description: A heading's text (any level, without '#'): return only its section.

name: list_pages
title: List pages
description: List the wiki's pages (slug, title, last edited, how many pages link to it), most recently edited first; with `under`, one folder's; with `orphans`, only pages no other page links to; with `notes`, only notes. Slugs show the folder structure.

under.description: Only pages in this folder and its subfolders, e.g. 'tickets' or 'projects' (the slug part before a '/').

orphans.description: Only pages no other page links to (the home page, the default task list's page and notes aside): candidates to link from somewhere.

notes.description: Only notes: the user's quick notes in Notes, named '<date>_<time>_<name>', not yet filed into the wiki.

name: check_links
title: Find broken links
description: List every link in the wiki, [[wikilink]] or markdown, that points to a page that doesn't exist, by page, with the existing page it was probably meant for.

under.description: Only pages in this folder and its subfolders, e.g. 'tickets'.

name: list_tags
title: List tags
description: List the tags in use, on pages (frontmatter tags:) and tasks, with how often each occurs. Check it before tagging, to reuse a tag instead of inventing a near-duplicate.

name: history
title: Show history
description: The wiki's git history. Without slug: recent changes across the wiki (what, when, which pages; '(MCP)' marks an assistant's), plus pages with changes not committed yet. With slug: that page's versions. With slug and version: what that version changed, as a diff. restore_page goes back to a version.

slug.description: A page, also a deleted one.

version.description: A version (commit) as history lists it, e.g. '1a2b3c4'.

since.description: Recent changes from this day on, YYYY-MM-DD.

under.description: Recent changes in this folder only, e.g. 'tickets'.

name: zone_help
title: Zone's documentation
description: Search Zone's own documentation (its README and its spec) for how Zone works: features, markdown syntax ([[tasks: …]] options, callouts, wikilinks, templates), the editor, search syntax, keyboard shortcuts, settings, setup, the MCP. Not the user's notes: search_wiki finds those. With query, the best passages; with topic (and heading), that doc or one section; with neither, the list of topics and their headings. The spec is written for Zone's developers: answer the user in terms of what they type or click, leaving out function and file names.

query.description: What to look for, in words the docs would use, e.g. 'tasks tab labels' or 'rename page'.

topic.description: A doc to read, as the results name it: 'readme', 'tasks', 'editor', 'navigation', …

heading.description: With topic: a heading's text, to read only its section.

limit.description: How many passages a query returns.

name: read_guides
title: Read the user's guides
description: Read the user's guides for a page or folder: their instructions for what goes there and how it is written (layout, tone, where it goes, what stays private). Call it before drafting anything meant for the wiki, before you write the first word, so the draft follows them. Returns each guide's text and its id. A page write under a guide (the wiki's, a folder's CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md) is refused until its id is in the write's guides; the refusal shows the guide and its id. Ids count for the conversation, until the user changes the guide.

slug.description: The page the content is meant for, also a new one ('messages/2026-10-11_reply'), or a folder ('messages/'). Leave it out for the whole wiki's guide.

guides.description: Ids of guides you already have in this conversation: they are named, not repeated.

name: read_file
title: Read an uploaded file
description: Read a file a page or task links to (an upload, '/_assets/…'): an image comes as an image, a text file as its text. For another kind (a PDF) or a big file, the answer says how to fetch it.

url.description: The link's target as written, e.g. '/_assets/photo.png'.

name: write_page
title: Create a page
description: Create a wiki page with the given markdown (start it with '# Title'). Fails if the page exists, unless overwrite, which replaces all of it; for part of a page, use edit_page or append_to_page. Names pages with similar names and wikilinks that lead nowhere. With note, a note instead: a quick note in the Notes module, for when the user wants something jotted down rather than filed in the wiki.

slug.description: The new page's slug or name, folders separated by '/', e.g. 'tickets/bug-1234' ('Tickets/BUG 1234' becomes that).

content.description: The page's full markdown. It may start with frontmatter: '---', then 'tags: a, b', 'tldr: one or two sentences' ('tldr: >' for several lines) and 'sources:' with one '- url', '- [label](url)' or '- [[page]]' line each, then '---'. Other keys are ignored.

base_hash.description: read_page's hash: merges a change made since.

note.description: Make a new note: slug is then just its name, in any words ('Alex prep'), and Zone puts the date and time in front.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: edit_page
title: Edit a page
description: Replace exact text in a page: old_string must match the page's markdown exactly (whitespace and line breaks included) and occur once, unless replace_all is true. Copy old_string from read_page or a search_wiki section. An empty new_string deletes the text. For several changes to one page, pass edits instead: applied in order, all or none, one commit.

slug.description: The page's slug as search_wiki or list_pages give it, e.g. 'git-remote' or 'journal/2026-09'.

edits.description: Instead of old_string/new_string: several replacements, each on the text the ones before it left. If one doesn't match, nothing is changed.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: replace_in_pages
title: Find and replace across pages
description: Replace text on every page where it occurs, in one commit: a term, a name, a ticket prefix, a link. Matched within a line; code (fenced blocks, inline code) is left alone unless include_code. Pages only, not tasks. By default a dry run that shows each line before and after and writes nothing: check it, then call again with dry_run=false. For changes to one page, use edit_page.

find.description: The text to find, within a line.

replace.description: What to put there; empty deletes. With regex, \1 or \g<name> are the groups.

regex.description: find is a regular expression (RE2 syntax: no lookarounds or backreferences).

include_code.description: Replace in code blocks and inline code too.

under.description: Only pages in this folder, e.g. 'tickets'.

dry_run.description: Only show what would change. false writes it.

max_pages.description: Refuse to write when more pages would change: a guard against a too broad find.

limit.description: How many changed lines a dry run shows.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: append_to_page
title: Append to a page
description: Add markdown to the end of a page, or with under_heading to the end of that heading's section (before the next heading of its level), without reading the page first. For logs and adding to a section.

slug.description: The page's slug as search_wiki or list_pages give it, e.g. 'git-remote' or 'journal/2026-09'.

under_heading.description: The heading whose section gets the text, e.g. 'Findings' (any level, case ignored). Leave it out to add at the end of the page.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: file_note
title: File a note
description: File a note (from Notes) into the wiki, as the user does from the note's menu: with name, move it there as its own page (folder/name); with page, append it to that page as a section and delete the note (its title goes, its headings move down, its tags join the page's). Either way links to the note follow.

name.description: Move to the wiki: the new page's name, e.g. 'Alex Sam debrief'.

folder.description: Move to the wiki: the folder it goes in, e.g. 'conversations'; none: the top level.

keep_date.description: Move to the wiki: keep the note's date in front of the name ('conversations/2026-10-15_alex-sam-debrief').

page.description: Append: the page to add the note to, e.g. 'people/alex'.

heading.description: Append: the section's heading; default the note's title and date, 'Alex prep (2026-10-15)'.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: upload_file
title: Upload a file
description: Add a file to the wiki's uploads (at most 1 MB here; the refusal of a bigger one says how to send it) and get the markdown that links it, to put on a page or in a task. A taken name gets a number; nothing is replaced.

content_base64.description: Any other file's bytes, base64. Give this or text.

page.description: The page it is for: a private page's file is private too.

name: rename_page
title: Rename or move a page
description: Rename a page or move it to another folder. Every link to it, on pages and in tasks, is changed to the new name. A folder ('projects/', with the slash) moves with all its pages and subfolders, in one commit.

slug.description: The page's slug as search_wiki or list_pages give it, e.g. 'git-remote' or 'journal/2026-09'. Or a folder, with a trailing slash: 'journal/'.

new_slug.description: The new slug, e.g. 'projects/leaf/mcp'; for a folder, the folder's new path.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: delete_page
title: Delete a page
description: Delete a page (it stays in the git history, restorable from Deleted Pages). Says which pages still link to it.

slug.description: The page's slug as search_wiki or list_pages give it, e.g. 'git-remote' or 'journal/2026-09'.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: restore_page
title: Restore a page version
description: Set a page back to an earlier version (history lists them), or bring back a deleted page. A new commit: the versions after it stay in the history.

slug.description: The page, also a deleted one.

version.description: The version to go back to, e.g. '1a2b3c4'.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

guides.description: Every guide id you have (read_guides); a write under a guide is refused without its id.

name: rename_task_tag
title: Rename a task tag or list
description: Rename a task tag, or a list (a tag a page declares): on all tasks, done ones too, and in embeds and /tasks links on pages, in one commit. Not pages' frontmatter tags.

merge.description: new_tag may be in use: the two merge.

name: create_task
title: Create a task
description: Add a task to the user's tasks. Returns it with its id, and the tags of similar tasks: offer the fitting ones to the user (update_task's add_tags adds them).

title.description: What to do, in a few words.

description.description: Markdown; replaces the one there is.

tags.description: The task's tags, without '#'. Replaces its tags; a list's name as a tag files it in that list.

importance.description: Shown before the title; normal unless said.

due.description: Deadline: YYYY-MM-DD, or today, tomorrow, a weekday (mon…sun: the next one) or +3d/+2w, which Zone resolves with its own date; empty to clear. A date the user gives the task ('tomorrow', 'by Friday', 'on the 3rd') goes here, not in start.

start.description: When to start working on it (it shows in Focus from then), as due takes dates; empty to clear. Only when the user says so ('start Monday', 'work on it tomorrow', 'plan it for Tuesday'); a plain date is the deadline (due).

repeat.description: Repeat the task; done, the next occurrence is created.

repeat_from.description: Next occurrence counted from the due date (default) or from when it was done.

keep.description: A keep task: done, it goes back to the list instead of being archived (shopping list staples).

assignee.description: With users: who does it: a user name, 'me' or 'none'. For 'Anna should …', not a tag.

private.description: With users: seen by the user alone. Default: private if their default task list (the first they pin) is in their private folder.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').

name: update_task
title: Update or comment on tasks
description: Change a task: only the fields given change. status: done (a repeating task gets its next occurrence), wont_do (close it undone: abandoned, or made by mistake; a task can't be deleted), skip (won't do this occurrence, the series goes on), open (reopen). comment adds a dated status line. With ids instead of id: add_tags/remove_tags on several tasks in one change. Case is ignored; list_tags shows the tags in use: reuse those.

id.description: The task's id as search_tasks or search_wiki show it (the 8-character short id is enough).

ids.description: Several tasks instead of id (ids or 8-character prefixes), for add_tags/remove_tags only.

description.description: Markdown; replaces the one there is.

tags.description: The task's tags, without '#'. Replaces its tags; a list's name as a tag files it in that list.

due.description: Deadline, as create_task takes it; empty to clear.

start.description: Start date, as create_task takes it (only when the user says so); empty to clear.

repeat.description: Repeat the task; done, the next occurrence is created.

repeat_from.description: Next occurrence counted from the due date (default) or from when it was done.

keep.description: A keep task: done, it goes back to the list instead of being archived (shopping list staples).

private.description: With users: false shares a private task; a shared one can't go private.

comment.description: A comment to add (markdown): a dated status line ('called Bob, waiting'), open or done tasks.

summary.description: The git commit message, a few words ('add findings from BUG-1234').
